Line movement uses directional deltas to assess whether sharp money supports or contradicts a pick—this is modeled as a signed scalar function of absolute change. The rest advantage component computes a bounded deviation in rest days between teams, flipping signs based on the pick side. Data quality introduces a multiplicative penalty that reduces model trust when inputs are sparse or stale. These primitives form a unified vector space where each dimension contributes to a final composite score. Dualities emerge in how line movement and rest advantage interact—e.g., a large negative spread may indicate strong home favoritism but also imply less rest for the away team. Failure modes include overfitting to noisy lines or ignoring venue-specific form. Uncertainty arises when multiple markets disagree, triggering a veto mechanism that downweights conflicting signals. This architecture ensures robustness through layered checks and adaptive weighting.
